::: {.hero-text}
# Lidio Jaimes Jr {.hero-name}

[Biostatistics Sc.M. -- Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health]{.hero-tagline}

I'm a biostatistics master's student at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, graduating in May 2027. I have a B.S. in Statistics from the University of Georgia.

At Johns Hopkins Medicine, I work on three cystic fibrosis studies, where I build R pipelines to automate study reports and handle quality control on longitudinal patient data. I'm also a graduate research assistant studying cognitive aging in older adults using the National Health and Aging Trends Study. This year, I'm a teaching assistant for three courses in the Department of Biostatistics.

Before Hopkins, I did research at the University of Georgia, UC Irvine, and Columbia on stroke outcomes, Alzheimer's disease in Down syndrome, and lung cancer costs. My work at UC Irvine led to a paper in *Alzheimer's & Dementia*, which I co-authored.

I work mainly in R, Python, SQL, and SAS, and I'm bilingual in English and Spanish. I'm looking for roles in data science, analytics, and statistics.

:::

### Neuropsychiatric symptoms and emerging dementia

Longitudinal analysis of 1,274 Down syndrome and 183,097 late-onset Alzheimer's visits. Co-author on the resulting paper in *Alzheimer's & Dementia* (2025).
